## Proof

**Claim:** Not every finitely presented group can be expressed as a quotient of the free group $F_2$ on two generators. In particular, $F_3$ (the free group on three generators) cannot be expressed as a quotient of $F_2$.

**Key observation.** Any quotient of $F_2$ is generated by at most two elements. Indeed, if $\pi: F_2 \to G$ is a surjective homomorphism, then $G$ is generated by the images $\pi(a), \pi(b)$ of the two free generators $a, b$ of $F_2$.

**$F_3$ is not generated by two elements.** Suppose for contradiction that $F_3$ is generated by two elements. Then its abelianization would also be generated by two elements. The abelianization of $F_3$ is $\mathbb{Z}^3$ (the free abelian group on three generators). But $\mathbb{Z}^3$ requires three generators: its rank as a free abelian group is $3$, which equals $\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{Z}^3 \otimes \mathbb{Q}) = 3$. A group generated by two elements has abelianization generated by at most two elements, hence has rank at most $2$. This is a contradiction.

**Conclusion.** Since every quotient of $F_2$ is generated by at most two elements, and $F_3$ requires three generators, $F_3$ cannot be a quotient of $F_2$. Therefore, not every finitely presented group can be expressed as a quotient of $F_2$.
